growing_tip.body_text: Beets | → Boro → Chioggia → Touchstone Gold → Avalanche → Red Ace (Pelleted) → 3 rows (11”-30 cm) per bed spaced every 5” (12 cm) on the row → Jang seeder: LJ-12 13F-10B, brush 1–3 mm, ≠ → Beets do best in beds amended with well-finished compost (rule of thumb is to spread compost ½ inch thick) but other amendments can supplement or replace it. Alternatively, we use a mix of alfalfa (2-0-2) meal and pelleted chicken manure (5-3-2). → Calcium and Boron are important nutrients for beets and Swiss chard. Without sufficient boron, beet growth suffers and the roots develop internal black spots | We plant beets every 3 weeks to ensure a constant supply of fresh beets with nice greens. For every seeding, we plan enough beds for an estimated 4 weeks of harvest per planting. → Rotary harrow → 30” bed prep rake → Direct Seeded: Individual Jang 3X seeder + LJ-12 roller, 5 markers for the rake, scale, notepad and your seeds → Transplant: Popping tray and dibbler/marking roller → Remove tarps and clean out any large debris. Use the rake if needed. * → Uniformly apply compost and or amendment and pass with the rotary harrow at a depth of 2” (5 cm). To make transplanting easier (seeing as the soil is loose after being harrowed), we only prepare the beds when we are about to transplant. → Pass with the dibbler roller to mark the planting holes and bring out the well-watered trays of transplants. → Once the beds are ready, 2 people begin to drop seedlings while another person starts to plant. Use the popping tray to facilitate extraction of seedlings. 3 people/100’ bed is a good ratio for efficient workflow. → While planting, pinch off extra heads if more than 1 seed has sprouted in the cell. → Install irrigation and water until the soil is well moistened. * If the previous crop is too well established, or if the bed is too messy, mow the crop as low as possible and harrow at a depth of 2” (5 cm). irrigation.body_text: → Drip tape (4 per bed) or sprinkler. | → Root depth: Medium (24”-40”) → General: Give adequate supply of water as lack during warm weather causes plants to bolt or beet roots to crack and/or become tough and woody. → General: Frequent shallow water to maintain flavor and succulence and support rapid growth. 1
